name: Serval and Colorful Array (Hard Version)
description: This is the hard version of the problem. The difference between the versions is that in this version, $$$n\le 4\cdot 10^5$$$. You can hack only if you solved all versions of this problem. Serval has a magic number $$$k$$$ ($$$k\ge 2$$$). We call an array $$$r$$$ colorful if and only if: The length of $$$r$$$ is $$$k$$$, and Each integer between $$$1$$$ and $$$k$$$ appears exactly once in $$$r$$$. You are given an array $$$a$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ integers between $$$1$$$ and $$$k$$$. It is guaranteed that each integer between $$$1$$$ and $$$k$$$ appears in $$$a$$$ at least once. You can perform the following operation on $$$a$$$: Choose an index $$$i$$$ ($$$1\le i \lt n$$$), then swap $$$a_i$$$ and $$$a_{i+1}$$$. Find the minimum number of operations needed to make at least one subarray$$$^{\text{∗}}$$$ of $$$a$$$ colorful . It can be shown that this is always possible under the constraints of the problem. $$$^{\text{∗}}$$$An array $$$b$$$ is a subarray of an array $$$a$$$ if $$$b$$$ can be obtained from $$$a$$$ by the deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the beginning and several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the end.
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 1000$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains two integers $$$n$$$ and $$$k$$$ ($$$2\leq k\leq n\leq 4\cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of the array $$$a$$$ and Serval's magic number. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_n$$$ ($$$1\leq a_i\leq k$$$) — the elements of the array $$$a$$$. It is guaranteed that each integer between $$$1$$$ and $$$k$$$ appears in $$$a$$$ at least once. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$4\cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum number of operations needed to make at least one subarray of $$$a$$$ colorful .
approach_summary: Build a Segment Tree over the array. Implement point update and associative range query operations in O(log N) time per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2085F2 — Serval and Colorful Array (Hard Version) [57. Segment Tree (Point Update Range Query)]
topic_editorial.summary: Range queries and updates via Segment Tree.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The query operation is associative (e.g., sum, min, max, gcd). Any contiguous range $[L, R]$ can be decomposed into at most $O(\log N)$ canonical dyadic intervals represented by nodes in a binary tree.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Tree Construction
We build a binary segment tree over array $A[1..N]$.
Each node covers a segment $[L, R]$. If $L = R$, the node stores $A[L]$. Otherwise:
$$\text{node.val} = \text{combine}(\text{left\_child.val}, \text{right\_child.val})$$

### Step 2: Point / Range Updates
To update position $pos$ with value $val$:
- Traverse down to the leaf node $[pos, pos]$.
- Update leaf value.
- Recompute ancestor values on the way back up in $O(\log N)$ time.

### Step 3: Range Query Processing
To query the associative aggregate on range $[qL, qR]$:
- If current segment $[L, R]$ is completely within $[qL, qR]$, return node value.
- If disjoint, return identity element.
- Otherwise, split and return $\text{combine}(\text{query}(left), \text{query}(right))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}((N + Q) \log N)$
  Building the segment tree takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$. Each point/range query and update traverses at most $4 \log N$ tree nodes, requiring $\mathcal{O}(\log N)$ time per query.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  A standard binary segment tree requires at most $4N$ nodes to represent elements up to index $N$.
